items.title: Chico Hamilton — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Well I was playing with Slam Stewart, Slim Gaillard in my freelance days

ctx.x: Well I was playing with Slam Stewart, Slim Gaillard in my freelance days, you know, but Ella -- I could phone my play in. If Ella said (musical sounds) at the end of the eighth bar, she’s going to do that every time so you know what it is, you know what I mean? Lena, you never knew what the hell she was going to do next, you know, what was she going to do. And she never sang anything in the same tempo twice. She could case a room man. She could case a room and she knew whether or not it should pick it up or slow…
Did you work in a large orchestra format or just the trio format?

items.title: Chico Hamilton interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 30, 2000

ctx.x: Man, Slim Gaillard was a genius. Was a pure genius. He was a drummer out there. And trombone player and scat singer by the name of Leo Watson. He was a genius. These guys, anything they touched, they made music with it. Slim Gaillard was unbelievable, unbelievable, unbelievable. He was fascinating. And you know Slam [Stewart], arco. But yeah that was — I was about 14, 15, 16, something like that.
Yeah. That’s wild. And everything of course, recordings back in those days, you were in a room and everybody played together.
